disposition_reason: The registered task estimates source ERP–prediction-error associations. Its coefficients and contrasts have no monotone scientific improvement direction. The existing coefficient-to-reference RMSE rewards numerical reconstruction; a proposed held-out choice log-loss task would change the endpoint and split.

source_paper.title: Separable neural signals for reward and emotion prediction errors

evidence.locator: Fig. 3; Methods: Participants, Psychophysiological recording and processing, Analyses; Data availability
evidence.supports: The paper tests dissociation of reward, valence and arousal PE associations with FRN/P3a/P3b and choices in 41 participants; it reports mixed-effects inference rather than a held-out ERP/choice prediction benchmark.

evidence.locator: Setup input tables; Figure 3 data bind_cols and fig3a_model, fig3b_model, fig3c_model
evidence.supports: Version-pinned author RMarkdown joins ERP tables to behavior by row order, filters missing valence predictions, uses source-scaled columns and fits separate mixed-effects ERP models.

Local scored endpoint is equal-model coefficient RMSE in reference standard errors, with fixed conditional REML models and row-order correspondence assumed. It explicitly disclaims independent improvement.

target.description: Distinct relationships of reward and emotion prediction errors with FRN, P3a and P3b amplitudes, and associations with subsequent social choices; registered central scope reconstructs the fixed mixed-effects coefficients and uncertainty.

dataset.description: Author processed behavior and ERP CSVs in 2025_epe_eeg at revision 4f5767df1516e0ec3c234d51ba36e4b741eb60e8; continuous cleaned EEG is a separate input level and raw-to-ERP reproduction is outside the registered numerical component.

cohort.description: 41 participants, 180 repeated Ultimatum Game trials each and 36 partners per participant. Author analyses exclude invalid/missing affect reports and use model-specific complete cases; the local contract counts 6,403 rows but this is not a published predictive test set.

split.description: The source central models fit the measured participant cohort with participant random effects. There is no published held-out participant/partner split for the registered coefficient-dissociation endpoint.

inputs.description: Trial reward and affect expectations/experiences, choices, participant identifiers, and extracted offer-locked FRN/P2/P3a/P3b and baseline ERP amplitudes. Source PE values are experience minus expectation.

preprocessing.description: 500-Hz EEG; average reference, eye-artifact correction, 0.1–40-Hz filtering, offer epochs −200–800 ms and artifact rejection. Single-trial windows: FRN 315–415 ms, P3a 363–463 ms and P3b 530–630 ms with source ROIs/covariates. PE standardization preserves meaningful zero; author CSV joins are positional.

metric.description: Source fixed-effect estimates and uncertainty for PE terms in participant mixed-effects ERP models, including contrasts across PE coefficients; these are inferential estimands, not a predictive accuracy target.

aggregation.description: Separate FRN/P3a/P3b models retain participant random effects over trials. Participant is the independent sampling unit; the local equal-model coefficient RMSE is only reference-reconstruction aggregation.

comparison.primary_metric: No ordered source-performance endpoint for the registered mixed-effects ERP coefficient dissociation.

published_baseline.description: The registered source estimands are biological measurements or associations, not an ordered algorithm-performance baseline. Numerical source findings must be reproduced or challenged on scientific grounds, not exceeded as a benchmark score.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: The qualified local numerical component scores equal-model coefficient RMSE normalized by reference coefficient standard errors for three fixed REML models, with secondary covariance/contrast consistency checks. These diagnose reconstruction, not better-than-paper neural prediction; all existing runs and references remain calibration evidence.

minimum_effect.rationale: No meaningful positive improvement margin is defined for this descriptive source target; greater effect size or stronger significance does not establish a better method.

uncertainty.method: No improvement-comparison uncertainty rule: this task is excluded from active performance improvement. Preserve the source analysis uncertainty when reproducing its estimands.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Participant (41), with repeated trials and partner interactions nested.
uncertainty.rationale: The source sampling hierarchy must not be converted into independent benchmark test examples. Descriptive uncertainty is not a rule for surpassing the paper.

paper_win_requires: The current registered descriptive target cannot admit a same-task paper-performance win.
Matching published values or the local numerical reference is calibration only.

A predictive or reconstruction endpoint with an ordered source baseline would require separately reviewed registration; a new split, narrowed cohort or changed endpoint is an extension, never a victory on this task.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison is claimed for this descriptive task.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive for this ineligible task; retain the original analysis as a calibration/reproduction component.
episode.candidate_freeze: No active improvement candidate is admitted. Any separately registered performance task must freeze its method and source-matched evaluation before final scoring.
episode.final_evaluation: No scientific improvement reward is issued from the existing descriptive or reference-reconstruction evaluator.
episode.baseline_policy: Preserve published descriptive results, any author reruns and local reconstruction references as distinct artifacts; none is promoted to a paper-performance baseline.

blocking_issues: The central source estimands are coefficient/contrast inference, not an ordered predictive benchmark.
No original held-out predictive split or source score exists for the proposed log-loss extension.
Independent ERP/behavior trial-key correspondence and continuous-to-ERP extraction provenance are not established by the positional CSV joins.

These diagnose reconstruction, not better-than-paper neural prediction; all existing runs and references remain calibration evidence.
